Key Research Thinking Patterns: Perception-Aware Adversarial Synthesis: Integrating human perceptual models with machine learning to generate adversarial examples that bypass detection systems while maintaining semantic or sensory fidelity. (e.g., Developing the CEMF-PA attack using a Siamese Neural Network trained on human perception data to manipulate pitch, rhythm, and timbre for bypassing YouTube copyright detection.)

Black-Box Reverse Engineering of Localization Algorithms: Exploiting the statistical dependencies in commercial geolocation services to infer hidden infrastructure data and execute spoofing attacks without physical-layer interference. (e.g., Formulating the LLT Inference Attack to extract precise Wi-Fi Access Point locations from Google's Location Lookup Table, enabling high-fidelity Wi-Fi location spoofing in urban environments.)

Proactive Defensive Deception via Signal Manipulation: Designing active countermeasures that inject controlled noise or fake signals to mislead eavesdroppers or attackers, rather than merely blocking access. (e.g., Implementing the HoneyBreath scheme using Software-Defined Radio to inject fake CSI-based breathing rates and crowd counts, deceiving classifiers with <1.2 bpm error and 100% success in empty room scenarios.)

Optimization-Driven Physical Layer Attack Formulation: Modeling security vulnerabilities as constrained optimization problems to minimize attack cost (e.g., energy) while maximizing success probability, validated through hardware-in-the-loop experiments. (e.g., Formulating the Identification Overriding (IDO) attack on RFID systems using Sequential Quadratic Programming to minimize injected signal energy, achieving 60-99% success rates on USRP X310 platforms.)
Summary Description: Shangqing Zhao is a principal investigator specializing in the intersection of machine learning, signal processing, and cybersecurity, with a focus on physical layer security and adversarial robustness. His research addresses critical vulnerabilities in audio content protection, geolocation services, and wireless communication systems. Key methodologies include perception-aware adversarial attack generation, black-box reverse engineering of commercial localization algorithms, and proactive defensive deception using software-defined radio. Zhao’s work spans from analyzing the security implications of Quantum Machine Learning on biomedical datasets to developing novel attacks and defenses for Wi-Fi, RFID, and vital sign monitoring systems. His contributions provide both theoretical frameworks and experimental validations for securing emerging technologies against sophisticated, signal-level threats, emphasizing the need for robust, perception-aware, and optimization-driven security mechanisms in IoT and mobile environments.
